Alammelech
uh-LAM-eh-lek
proper noun
A town in the inheritance of the tribe of Asher, named in the roll of its cities; the name is taken to mean “oak of the king” or, in its ending, “the king” — a witness to the kingship of God.

📖 Biblical Definition

Alammelech was a town in the inheritance of Asher, named among that tribe’s cities: “And Alammelech, and Amad, and Misheal” (Jos 19:26). It is named nowhere else. The name is taken to mean oak of the king, and its ending carries the word melech, king. A town bearing the King’s name, set in the portion of Asher, quietly confesses the great truth that God is King — not king of Israel only, but King of all the earth. “For God is the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding” (Psa 47:7). The nations rage and the peoples imagine a vain thing, but He that sitteth in the heavens laughs; He has set His King upon His holy hill of Zion, and given Him the heathen for His inheritance. To Him belongs the everlasting dominion: “Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever” (1Ti 1:17). The believer, whose citizenship is in a kingdom that cannot be moved, owns Christ as King of kings and Lord of lords, and bows the knee gladly to Him whom the Father has crowned. A little oak-town of Asher, carrying the King’s name upon it, is a standing witness that the LORD reigns, and shall reign for ever and ever, and of His kingdom there shall be no end.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Asher whose name ends in “king”; a witness to the kingship of God, who is King of all the earth and reigneth for ever.

ALAMMELECH, a town in the inheritance of Asher.

It is named among that tribe’s cities (Jos 19:26).

The name is taken to mean oak of the king.

Its ending carries the word melech, king.

It witnesses to the kingship of God, King of all the earth.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 19:26 — "And Alammelech, and Amad, and Misheal; and reacheth to Carmel westward, and to Shihorlibnath;"

Psa 47:7 — "For God is the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding."

1Ti 1:17 — "Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen."

Psa 93:1 — "The LORD reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the LORD is clothed with strength, wherewith he hath girded himself: the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A town of Scripture whose name confesses the King; it recovers the truth that God is King of all the earth, and Christ the King eternal reigns for ever.

expand to see more

Alammelech faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name confesses answers the rebellious spirit of the age, which will own no king but self, and casts off the cords of the Lord’s anointed, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the kingship of God. A town of Asher carrying the King’s name witnesses that the LORD is King of all the earth; the nations rage in vain, for He has set His King upon Zion. The believer owns Christ as King eternal, and of His kingdom there shall be no end.
